original_question: Extend the theory of virtual covers so that it applies effectively to classical knots in S^3, relate virtual-cover invariants to Milnor mu-invariants and possibly to one-component links, understand how virtual covers behave under local moves such as crossing changes, self-Delta moves, and Z-moves, determine whether virtual covers can detect mutations, and characterize exactly which moves on two-component links preserve the associated virtual-knot type.
target_in_paper: Section 8.5.3, "Connections between classical and virtual knot theory," specifically the five numbered open problems on virtual covers (items 1-5) in Micah W. Chrisman's question list.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the paper's virtual-cover problem cluster very closely. It includes all of the main themes of items 1-5 in Section 8.5.3: extending virtual covers from links in S^3 with at least two components to knots in S^3; relating Milnor mu-invariants to invariants of virtual knots and to one-component links; studying behavior under crossing changes, self-Delta moves, and Z-moves; asking about mutation detection; and classifying moves on two-component links that preserve the associated virtual-knot type.
missing_details: The paper first fixes the setup of a virtual cover: N is a compact oriented 3-manifold, K is a smooth knot in N, Pi: Sigma x (0,1) -> N is a covering space, and k is a smooth knot in Sigma x (0,1) with Pi(k)=K; the associated virtual knot upsilon is obtained by viewing k in Sigma x [0,1] and projecting to a virtual knot.
The paper defines a fundamental virtual cover as the case where Pi is regular and k lies in a fundamental region of Pi.

Problem 1 is specifically about extending a theory that currently studies links in S^3 with at least two components to one-component links, i.e. knots, in S^3; the word "effectively" is not part of the paper's formulation.

Problem 2 asks for a relation between Milnor mu-invariants and invariants of virtual knots, and then explicitly asks whether virtual covers can be used to apply Milnor's theory to one-component links (knots); "virtual-cover invariants" is broader than the paper's wording.
Problem 3 concerns the virtual knot associated to a virtual cover of a classical link under local non-isotopy moves applied to that link.
Problem 4 asks specifically whether virtual covers can detect mutations of classical links.

Problem 5 has essential hypotheses and quantifiers omitted in the draft: every virtual knot upsilon is the associated virtual knot of a fundamental virtual cover of some two-component link K ⊔ J, where J is fibered and lk(J,K)=0; the required classification is of moves on such links that preserve the virtual isotopy type of the associated virtual knot.
In the paper these are posed as five separate open problems within one subsection, not as a single generalized research program.
refined_question: In the setting of a virtual cover (k in Sigma x (0,1), Pi, K_N) of a smooth knot K in a compact oriented 3-manifold N, where Pi: Sigma x (0,1) -> N is a covering space, Pi(k)=K, the associated virtual knot upsilon is obtained from k viewed in Sigma x [0,1], and the cover is fundamental when Pi is regular and k lies in a fundamental region, determine to what extent the virtual-cover construction for links in S^3 with at least two components can be extended to one-component links (knots) in S^3; whether one can relate Milnor mu-invariants to invariants of the associated virtual knot and thereby apply Milnor's theory to knots; how the associated virtual knot changes under local non-isotopy moves on a classical link, especially crossing changes, self-Delta moves, and Z-moves; whether virtual covers can detect mutation of classical links; and, using the fact that every virtual knot upsilon arises as the associated virtual knot of a fundamental virtual cover of some two-component link K ⊔ J with J fibered and lk(J,K)=0, find a complete set of moves on such links that preserve the virtual isotopy type of upsilon.
justification: The draft clearly does not target the early Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 material; instead it matches, almost item for item, the virtual-cover open problems in Section 8.5.3. The paragraph immediately preceding the numbered list gives the exact local notation and hidden assumptions needed to make the question stand alone: the definitions of virtual cover, associated virtual knot, and fundamental virtual cover, plus the scope in which the theory had already been studied. Item 5 also contains a crucial quantifier and hypotheses absent from the draft: every virtual knot arises from a fundamental virtual cover of some two-component link K ⊔ J with J fibered and lk(J,K)=0. Because your draft omits the adjacent primeness problem (item 6), the closest paper-faithful target is precisely items 1-5 of Section 8.5.3.
